metadata.title: Synthetic: DRL and Imitation Learning for Power Grid Voltage Control

blocks.text: 1 Introduction

Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been applied to autonomous voltage control of power grids. Both value-based algorithms (i.e., DQN) and policy gradient algorithms (i.e., DDPG) have been studied in previous work.

Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been applied to autonomous voltage control of power grids. Both value-based algorithms (i.e., DQN) and policy gradient algorithms (i.e., DDPG) have been studied in previous work.
2 Method

In this work we use soft actor-critic (SAC) as the policy gradient algorithm because it encourages exploration. We further propose an imitation learning approach that is trained only on successful steps collected from a random policy.
4 Results
Fig. 1 compares the number of unsolvable cases for the SAC agent and the imitation learning agent on the test set.

metadata.title: Synthetic: A DRL Approach for Ramp Metering

blocks.text: Related Works
Classical ramp metering strategies such as ALINEA regulate on-ramp flows using point detector measurements. PI-ALINEA extends ALINEA with a proportional-integral term for downstream bottlenecks.
Methodology
The deep Q-learning agent is trained with experience replay and a target network that is updated after a fixed freezing interval.
Case study

Fig. 8 presents the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios. The proposed DRL method reduces the mean travel time by 13% compared with the no-control scenario, while PI-ALINEA reduces it by 9%.
References

1. Papageorgiou, M., H. Hadj-Salem, and J.M. Blosseville, ALINEA: A local feedback control law for on-ramp metering. Transportation Research Record, 1991. 1320 (1): p. 58-67. 2. Wang, Y., et al., Local ramp metering in the presence of a distant downstream bottleneck: Theoretical analysis and simulation study. IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, 2014. 15 (5): p. 2024-2039.
